Research Toolkit

English · 简体中文

Turn a research question or existing material into a report with concrete judgments and traceable sources.

Use it for industry research, product comparisons, company analysis and technical research. Start a new study, revise an existing report against its sources, or update conclusions when new material arrives. Your agent researches and writes; Toolkit supplies the methods and optional workflow tools.

Choose an entry · Start research · See a research case · Documentation

Research capabilities cover task/context, evidence/analysis, writing/revision and review/delivery. The lead continues research and assembly; independent questions can be delegated for analysis, calculation and local writing. See collaboration and actual requests.

Which should I use?

The Skill provides research methods, CLI and MCP expose the same local tools, and the plugin bundles the Skill with MCP. These are not four research methods or separate choices for briefs, long reports or research depth.

Your situation What to use or install How to start
You want your existing agent to follow the research methods Skill: read the repository directly without installation, or install the Skill for repeated use. No Python or MCP required. Send the request below; the agent reads methods as needed and uses its existing research and writing capabilities.
You want methods and task tools together, and your host supports plugins Plugin: installs the Skill and MCP together; local tools need Python 3.10+ and MCP dependencies. Follow the plugin instructions, reopen the session, select Toolkit and describe the research.
You need saved task state, recovery and links between sources and drafts, and your host supports local MCP MCP: configure the local service and use the same Skill for methods. No separate MCP setup is needed if the plugin already supplies it. Follow the MCP setup; the agent calls research_* tools.
You work in a terminal or script, or your host has no MCP support CLI: download the repository and use Python 3.10+; no MCP dependencies needed. The agent reads the same Skill and invokes the same task tools through the command line.

For a first use, start directly with the Skill. Add task tools when persistent state, tool-managed reviews or delivery checks help the work, not because a report reaches a word count. You do not need to install all four or use them in sequence. Skill-only use supports in-depth long reports without requiring the tools' CSV/JSONL registries or delivery receipts.

Which tasks fit? Industry, company, technology and policy research requiring multiple sources, comparison, explanation or supported recommendations; long reports, revisions and continuing updates. A one-page selection brief can need these methods too. Simple factual questions, routine translation or minor wording edits usually need only your existing agent. Toolkit does not supply a search service or replace the agent's access to and reading of sources.

Research from scratch · Revise or update a report · Install for your host

Quick start

Describe your question or requested revision in your own words to an agent that can read the repository and sources. The example below is a starting point; you do not need to fill in undecided details. The agent uses existing context to propose an approach and clarifies only consequential gaps. No installation is needed to use the methods directly.

Use Research Toolkit: https://github.com/rrrrrredy/research-toolkit
Read SKILL.md and follow the methods needed for this task.

I want to understand or resolve: [The question, or what to change in an existing report.]
Audience and purpose: [Who will read it and why, if known.]
Material and explicit requirements: [Sources, scope, cutoff, format or length, if available.]

Deliver a complete report that answers these questions with usable citations;
include a short change note when revising.

Start research: one usage guide

One method set supports long-form and in-depth research, revisions and updates. The request determines scope, length and depth; the agent loads methods as needed and completes agreed checks.

Only need to review an existing report? Use the standalone Research Review Skill. Toolkit already includes these review capabilities; existing users do not need a second installation.

Have a draft or new material? Revise or update existing research, reusing completed research and its sources.

Research case

APIs or browsers for AI agents. An English report drawing on 11 primary sources to compare API calls, DOM automation and visual interaction through completion, recovery and cost.

Read the report · Initial draft · Sources · Reviews and revisions

A revision that changes the decision

Before:

There is no benefit in preserving this split if the API later covers document generation with adequate permissions and result checking.

After:

If the API later covers document generation with adequate permissions and result checking, the original coverage gap disappears. Retiring the browser step then depends on whether the expected maintenance and recovery savings justify migration and revalidation costs.

The review identified a missing counterexample: replacing a working browser step may cost more than the expected savings. The revision makes that trade-off part of the recommendation.

Explore the revision

Public-source analysis dated 10 October 2026, not a deployment test. Also read the Chinese office-agent comparison and its source and revision archive.

Agent setup

How you want to use it Entry
Read the methods directly Send the request above; for files or text-only chats, see agent setup.
Install a Skill or plugin Choose your agent · Plugin installation
Save progress and call workflow tools MCP installation and client configuration · CLI
Try the local tools Runnable MCP example and captured responses; replays a supplied self-review without an external model call.

The nine local tools manage task records, stage guidance, registered release-log queries, reviews and delivery checks. MCP needs Python 3.10+ and a client that can start a local process; the installation guide covers Windows, macOS and Linux.

Reviews support author-context self, a configured external backend, or independent review in a separate context. Astra can provide independent review without an outside person or another vendor. State the tier actually used; an explicit independent-review requirement cannot be silently downgraded. Review configuration

Evidence and evaluations

Public records include complete reports, original failures, reviews and repairs. They show concrete report corrections and tested workflow behavior; they do not yet establish a general quality or efficiency advantage over a native agent. Case studies, model comparisons and software checks answer different questions.
